content: I would rather die having spoken after my manner, than speak in your manner and live.
author: Socrates
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Across his life and work, Socrates saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: What current difficulty or obstacle are you facing that could become your greatest training ground?
